text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert — sustained TLS handshake latency and streaming tail stalls in EU regions. p95 for handshake time rose from ~95ms -> ~1.0s and p99 hit ~4.2s. Stream session stalls and retransmit counters climbing on cross-AZ/eu-west2 -> eu-central paths. Paging toro (on-call).

toro (on-call): acknowledging. quick state: is this NAT/conntrack again or something different? where's the spike starting and what components show errors?

netops: seeing correlated route table churn in the VPC peerings between eu-west2 AZ-b and eu-central AZ-a starting 2003001140. Route propagation shows brief withdraw/restore cycles for some egress subnets. Traceroutes from load-balancers show an extra hop (10.254.77.1) intermittently.

kevin: checked conntrack/tcp states on nat-eu-west2-3: conntrack at ~35% (not the bottleneck). However, TCP retransmits and SYN retries on the egress path increased ~6x. I suspect packet loss or asymmetric routing causing handshake RTTs to balloon, not pure conntrack exhaustion.

maria-sre: streaming runtime telemetry: worker handshake queue depth spiked at 2003001155, backlog caused chunk emission stalls (clients get long gaps between chunks). Aggregated client-side reconnects up by 12%.

jamie-pm: any customer-visible errors? which customers most impacted?

customer-ops: customers D and E reported streaming stalls and longer first-byte times. No full session failures, more user-perceived sluggishness. Drafting a short notice: "We're investigating intermittent network latency affecting streaming in EU regions; working on mitigations."

toro (on-call): mitigation plan: 1) address route instability (netops to hold routes steady), 2) reduce handshake pressure (enable longer keepalives + handshake threadpool bump), 3) short-term traffic steering to healthy AZs for streaming traffic. Execute canary for 5% first.

netops: running route table pin to prefer local egress for LB subnets and disabling route propagation for the flapping peer while we investigate. Command run: ```aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abc1234 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --gateway-id nat-rtb-eu-west2-local``` Monitoring.

alice-fw: noted unusual packet dupes and out-of-order on tcpdump samples; applied an ingress ACL to rate-limit bursts from a small set of client IPs causing connection churn. Rule will be live for 10m. `iptables -I PREROUTING -m limit --limit 200/s -j ACCEPT` applied on edge node.

eng-runtime: we'll flip a runtime knob to increase TLS handshake worker threads so handshakes don't block the core emitter threads. Applying to streaming pool: `kubectl patch deployment runtime-stream -p '{"spec": {"template": {"spec": {"containers": [{"name":"stream","env":[{"name":"TLS_HANDSHAKE_THREADS","value":"32"}]}]}}}}'` Doing canary to 3 pods.

kevin: after route pin, traceroute stabilized and retransmits dropped ~70%. SYN retry rate dropped accordingly. p95 handshake fell to ~330ms within 90s.

maria-sre: runtime handshake-queue normalized on canary pods. Stream chunk intervals back to expected. Observed a small increase in reconnects during steer but overall client experience improving.

toro (on-call): starting streaming routing canary to prefer eu-west2-A/healthy AZ for 5% of EU traffic. Watch p95/p99 and streaming stall rate. If p99 < 700ms for 2m, widen to 25%.

incident-bot: automated note — pager cleared by toro at 2003001405. Incident remains P1 until service-level metrics meet SLOs.

jamie-pm: customer-ops notify customers with timeline and mitigations; include that we're doing route stability fixes + runtime changes.

customer-ops: message sent. Customers acknowledged; asking for follow-up RCA and whether this could recur.

sre-lead: good work. followups: investigate root cause of route propagation flaps (cloud provider routing, peering, or control-plane bug), add guardrails to prevent route thrash, and add an alert on route-update rate for core subnets. Assigning to netops + kevin.

kevin: collecting artifacts: BGP/route change logs, `tcpdump -c 2000 -w /tmp/nat-eu-west2-3-sample.pcap`, and LB telemetry for the 2003001080-2003001220 window. Uploading to incident-bucket/inc-4890/

netops: found noisy health-checks from a misconfigured antiscan job in an internal account that triggered route recalculation in the cloud peer (health check flapping feedback loop). We've disabled that job and promoted stable route table entries.

alice-fw: removed temporary rate-limit rule after 8m; no regression observed. Will move rule to managed firewall group for future quick toggles.

maria-sre: creating INC-4890: "Intermittent VPC route propagation -> TLS handshake tail latency and streaming stalls". Action items: provider-support ticket for route propagation, add route-change alerting, runtime knob default increase, client SDK guidance for keepalive.

eng-runtime: will add a dashboard panel for handshake queue length and threadpool saturation and propose default TLS_HANDSHAKE_THREADS=24 in runtime images.

toro (on-call): routing canary widened to 25%. Observed p95=160ms, p99=480ms, streaming stall rate back to baseline. Marking mitigation achieved at 2003001588.

sre-lead: schedule RCA meeting for tomorrow 09:00 UTC. Primary owners: netops (route root cause), eng-runtime (backpressure hardening), alice-fw (rate-limiting playbook), customer-ops (customer comms). Postmortem ticket INC-4890 created.

incident-bot: Incident summary queued for #postmortems. Tags: networking, vpc-routing, tls, streaming, p99.

toro (on-call): wrapping up — handing to kevin/netops for RCA. I'm off-call. Nice collaboration team. :thumbsup:

kevin: will correlate with control-plane event logs and prepare RCA notes. Expect initial draft in INC-4890 today.

customer-ops: customers updated; they requested ETA for permanent mitigations — we'll include in postmortem.

sre-lead: thanks all. prioritized follow-ups: route-change alerts, runtime defaults, firewall quick-actions, and provider escalation. Close thread after RCA posted."
